text:
Sam: Heads-up, eu-west incident this morning. Region kept being preferred by the proxy despite prolonged queueing on GPU nodes. Anyone seen traces?

Anya: saw alerts. the priority score barely moved when queues rose — it only factors instantaneous latency, not sustained backlog.

Kevin: dug into traces: one old model shard had p99 spikes and a couple of OOM-restarts. proxy timeout of 6s lets requests accumulate and dilutes the impact of 5xx in the score.

Maria: 6s is too lenient for interactive routes. p99-sensitive routes need faster failure detection.

Lucas: agree but cautious: too-aggressive timeouts will flip primaries for transient blips. we need hysteresis + safety window.

Sam: proposed heuristic (draft):
```
priority = base_score
priority -= weight_5xx * recent_5xx_rate
priority -= clamp(lat_ms, 0, 2000) / 40
priority -= decay_by(window_seconds)

# demote when sustained_5xx > 0.15 for 30s OR priority < threshold for 45s
# prefer warm-standby targets; respect tenant residency consent before redirecting writes
```

Kevin: change list for canary:
- reduce proxy connect+read timeout -> 3s (was 6s)
- require 30s sustained signal before demotion
- increase 5xx weight so hard errors dominate
- emit metrics: redwood.region_priority_score, redwood.demote_candidate (per-tenant)

Maria: add alerts: page if demote_count > 3/min for any region + heatmap dashboard for region_priority_score. also add suppress window to avoid alert storms during rollout.

Anya: residency constraint: for tenants with fixed residency or regulatory flags, demotion flow must not forward writes cross-region. reads OK if policy allows. We need an explicit consent check.

Sam: residency demote checklist: 1) check tenant.residency.policy (fixed|soft|multi) 2) if policy!=multisite and request.is_mutation => abort demote, return local 5xx fallback or queued degrade 3) if soft and consent==true => allow cross-region read/write per consent table 4) ensure warm-standby has prefix cache or use cache-warmup tag

Lucas: edge-case: quick timeouts + in-flight retries can cause duplicate work and KV cache clobber. Suggest inserting dedupe header: X-Redwood-Dedupe: <uuid>. Backends detect duplicates within 3s window and can short-circuit duplicate writes.

Kevin: add exponential jittered backoff on re-route attempts: base 150ms * 2^n capped at 2s, with ±20% jitter. prevents thundering and gives backend time to recover.

Sam: test plan: canary 100 tenants in eu-west for 2 hours with proxy-config:v43. Collect demote_count, reroute_rate, per-tenant 5xx, end-to-end p95/p99. Compare false-positive demotes vs baseline.

deploybot: deploybot: starting canary rollout proxy-config:v43 -> eu-west (100 tenants) at 2026-03-21T18:12:44Z :rocket:

Maria: I'll wire dashboards + alerts (demote_count, region_priority_score heatmap, dedupe-detect-rate). Also add a suppression rule during rollout.

Anya: quick nit: in the heuristic math, make decay window configurable per tier — lower tiers can have faster decay to avoid being stuck.

Sam: good — I'll open follow-up RFC with config snippet and residency decision table, tagging @Anya @Kevin for review. We'll include example headers and canary dashboard links.

Kevin: once canary completes, validate no cross-region writes for fixed-residency tenants and roll metrics back to baseline before wider rollout.

Lucas: +1. Also add operator runaway guard: if demote_count spikes unexpectedly, auto-pause demotion heuristic and escalate to oncall.

Sam: sounds good. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
